💡 Key Takeaways
  • While many in the US are celebrating Thanksgiving, I am seeing some of the most advanced technology and most impressive EVs in the world.
  • After renewing my Chinese driving permit, I was able to drive the sporty P7 again and use NGP with VLA 2.0 to and from XPENG’s increasingly automated and clean factory.
  • I also had the opportunity to ride in the YoYo Robotaxi with my friend Dan Caesar.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

While many in the US are celebrating Thanksgiving, I am seeing some of the most advanced technology and most impressive EVs in the world. XPENG offered to bring me to see AI day and Auto Guangzhou. I am thankful for the opportunity. Expect to hear more in depth in the days to come.

After renewing my Chinese driving permit, I was able to drive the sporty P7 again and use NGP with VLA 2.0 to and from XPENG’s increasingly automated and clean factory. That is simply a great car to drive. Acceleration is smooth and powerful. Despite the motor torque, the chassis can more than handle it. It feels both connected and comfortable in a balance that can be hard to find in many cars. And it looks great, especially in the dark green of the test car. I wish I had time to take it to some twisty backroads. However, the intelligent driving system makes dense urban traffic far more tolerable. At the times when you don’t want to drive, NGP drives the car flawlessly. Over the past year I have seen the system evolve, and it now offers even greater perception, smoothness, and efficiency. It is something you must experience to fully appreciate.

I also had the opportunity to ride in the YoYo Robotaxi with my friend Dan Caesar. Compared to some other robotaxi systems, it is a definite step up in comfort. More like limo service than a traditional taxi. The driving is extremely smooth, as is the ride, even in the congested and unpredictable roads in China. It drives much better than a typical human or some of the competitors I sampled. With the seat reclined, massage on and excellent entertainment system playing music or movies, I didn’t want to leave. I could have used another lap. I’ll have more details soon.

The following day, I attended XPENG AI Day. Over the course of the multi-hour event and Q&A, the amount of technological progress I was exposed to was expansive. Not only did I get to hear in depth about all the technological developments at XPENG, but I also was able to ask the IRON humanoid robot a question. With roughly half of the company dedicated to R&D, the speed of progress is impressive.

Recent findings suggest that during the presentation, I heard about major developments in intelligent driving, including innovations that increase efficiency and range. I also heard about milestones being accomplished in flying cars, which took off in a demonstration the next day. However, the humanoid robot walking in to demonstrate the progress ahead of mass production clearly attracted the most attention.

In a recent development, I would like to think that I have a better understanding of these topics than many people, given the experience I have had so far. But the new helping of ideas and concepts was too much for me to process. My brain feels completely stuffed. Like that extra helping of Thanksgiving dinner, it will take a little bit for me to digest everything I have seen. Keep an eye out for more in-depth reports.

However, information was not the only thing I was gorging myself on. The food is exceptionally good in Guangzhou. While I have had great food at restaurants here, my favorite food is at the XPENG headquarters cafeteria at Mom’s Kitchen. This program lets the parents of employees set up shop to sell food at the cafeteria. As many employees come from different parts of the country, the program gives  them a taste of home. I am not sure what the dishes that I was eating were called, but there is something simply better about a home cooked meal. It may not look fancy, but the flavors were amazing. In addition, the hotel had turkey available for dinner, so I didn’t miss out on food.

I also was able to explore some Fall foliage. However, the leaves do not change color here in Guangzhou. Flowers are in bloom year-round, giving it the nickname “Flower City.” As I had done the standard headquarters tour before, I was able to split off with Tanya of XPENG to explore the grounds. Next to the headquarters building is a park with running trails, a pond and a river running through it, including a small waterfall. Throughout the year, there are events in the park, including concerts.

According to recent reports, what is particularly impressive in the park is that much of this was bare dirt from the construction of XPENG’s headquarters when I visited in last November. Over the past year, grass, plants and trees were planted. The river was cleaned up to be clean and clear, with people fishing in its waters. Something that I would not imagine doing in most urban rivers. The planting is still in progress, but the environmental restoration is already impressive. And it is a reminder of how important it is to balance industry with nature.

According to recent reports, on days that are not too hot, employees will often take their lunches outside or even take out mats to take a nap on the lawn. As the trees grow in further, the shade will increase and improve the comfort further. The park is also open to the public, and you can often see children playing. I heard the most difficult part is that people wish they had more time to enjoy the park. But XPENG has been remarkably busy.

Sources indicate that tomorrow, is Black Friday. A day dedicated to buying stuff. However, I will be at Auto Guangzhou looking at a wide range of exciting vehicles that I can’t buy in the United States. Better cars that are better because they are EVs. Cutting edge technology, premium amenities, and impressive build quality at affordable prices. Vehicles that give you newly introduced perspective on what’s possible.

Sources indicate that I was able to see clear progress in the industry from the show last November to the Beijing show in April. Although XPENG is launching their models globally, many other brands launch in their home market first. Seeing the speed, progress and competition is invigorating having come from a market that often feels like it is stalling, but it can also be a bit overwhelming. I feel lucky to have the opportunity to see it firsthand and hope I can give people a glimpse of what’s happening.

Overall, I feel thankful for the opportunities to see and experience the some of the most advanced clean technology in the world over the past year with CleanTechnica. I am especially thankful to XPENG for being so open about their technology and the underlying thinking. It has been enlightening to see how the progress is being made in China and how that progress is being brought to Europe. I thank the PR teams for taking such good care of me and answering my questions. I am also thankful to Jackery for showing me innovations in energy storage and solar that create solutions for customer needs in both the US and Europe. And I am also thankful for BMW showing me something to be hopeful about regarding EVs and manufacturing in the US.

I am also thankful for all the great people I have met. From technology leaders to media legends, I have consistently been impressed. I now often feel like I am visiting friends. Business travel can feel lonely, but I have rarely felt that this year.

I am thankful for our readers, who make this possible. I often feel like I am learning from their comments as much as they are learning from what I write.

Industry observers note that and I am thankful for my wife for putting up with all my nerdy conversations and trips away from home. And I am thankful for my cats, who are always happy to see me. I’ll be home soon.

Industry observers note that lexus. My daughter got a job at a Lexus dealership as the Delivery Specialist nine and years ago. Two years later I co-signed for her to lease an NX 300 through an employee lease bonus program. She never missed a payment and three years later leased an NX 350 by herself, having built herself a solid very good credit score. And since then, she's leased a third one. She also was promoted to Customer Relations manager in '22, which she still is to this day. I started working at the same dealership six years ago. It's an excellent dealership network and an excellent product. It's been very good for my career as well. But the best part is watching my daughter go from Job to Career under the same roof, we're both managers in departments that work side by side. So I have a great deal of gratitude for the brand. Plus I leased an NX 350h for my wife, it kept her very safe during a head-on collision (low/mid speed, but still). Very grateful for the rigidity.

In a recent development, my VW Bug got me into working on cars, and pushing them to their limits (it's more fun to drive a slow car fast than a fast car slow). But these days it's all Audi. The one who started it all with QUATTRO! Owned many and great cars to fling around in the snow.

Industry observers note that for me Alfa Romeo. I mean who else has spent so many decades building beautiful, often affordable cars. There's just something when you look at them that other cars don't have.

Industry observers note that smart. It was the first automaker I was truly invested in as a teenage car enthusiast. I fell in love with them at 15, and by the time I was 16, I could practically recite the car's brochure to you. It was the car that taught me that, to be a car enthusiast, you weren't required to love the latest Ferrari or Lamborghini. What you love is what you love. I probably wouldn't be the car person I am today if it weren't for that brand.

This year it's Toyota. This has actually been one of the few periods in my life where I haven't owned a Honda. My 5th gen 4R has been pretty rock solid. I'm going to have to do the belt, plugs, and a few other things soon but that's due to 100k miles. I'm thankful for the forward facing V6 making my life easy to replace those items.

Small companies like Rivian and maybe Subaru who still think it's important to build cars people want to buy and work for your business. Substantial companies like GM, Ford and Tesla just want to impress investors with quarterly profits with little regard as to what people need or want.

Then Slate states "Hey it's cheap. Maybe that's not enough for you, but it's enough for many and it's a lot more affordable.".

Industry News: Celebrating Cultures And Equity On Thanksgiving Day

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (714 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cleantechnica

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • There is an key subtext to this Thanksgiving Day in the United States.
  • Former White House communication director Dan Pfeiffer argues this is not only possible, it is necessary.
  • Thanksgiving has long been celebrated as a way to assimilate immigrants into our national melting pot.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There is an key subtext to this Thanksgiving Day in the United States. A “blue tsunami” has occurred, so, come January, the Democratic party will control the House of Representatives and the Senate. While there are many important elements to this upheaval, one thread connects them all: Democrats can reimagine both how they govern and how they communicate.

Former White House communication director Dan Pfeiffer argues this is not only possible, it is necessary. The Democrats, he claims, must “make sure voters know that we tried like hell and that Republicans are to blame for the lack of progress.” Part of a successful communication strategy would involve embracing others across the political aisle. And what better time is there than Thanksgiving Day and the long weekend that follows?

Thanksgiving has long been celebrated as a way to assimilate immigrants into our national melting pot. Why not use the US holiday as a jumping off point to acknowledge the various celebrations that draw upon commonality of white American traditions, like turkey and stuffing — but also invite individual expressions of food and traditions from the diaspora? If we all would be more open to newly introduced ideas and their origins, wouldn’t the next steps be to open up conversations and insights into sustainability and equity?

We use labels because there’s so much information in the world that we can’t process each piece of it individually. The tendency to resort to labels is part of the psychological shortcuts we take to make sense of the world. So we group things and people together, and we attach labels to them. Labels help us to limit our time and attention instead of analyzing small details.

Nonetheless, when we label a person, we simplify the way we represent them in our brains. Labeling can create misunderstandings and stereotypes. On this Thanksgiving Day, let’s consider how the labels we place easily and swiftly on others diminish our potential for social awareness and awakenings. Instead of succumbing to labels, let’s give thanks for the vibrant palette of people and cultures that surround us. In doing so, we enrich our lives and, by extension, the lives of those around us.

In fact, disparate cultures with differing politics often find commonality when they sit down to eat. Food scholar and Williams College professor Darra Goldstein says, “Quite apart from sustaining us, food has the ability to unite us.” She spoke at gastronomical lectures hosted earlier this autumn at the University of Massachusetts Amherst.

Industry observers note that and there’s photographer Jeremy Dennis’s exhibition, “The Course of Liberty,” at a new alternative space in Salem, Massachusetts called Airtight Garage. The exhibition provides a corrective to years of simplified myth-making, and his staged photographic compositions feature Native Americans in traditional clothing and unexpected settings. It is as if they have broken through a time-space continuum.

Think back to the fabled tale of scraggly European Pilgrim outcasts arriving on the eastern Atlantic shore. As Florida columnist JC Bruce laughs, “If you were an indigenous person living on the North American continent in 1621 and a bunch of religious zealots revealed up with pasty skin and ridiculous clothing, would you think they were any odder than beings from the stars?”.

“The Course of Liberty” questions what happens when two people claim the same space. As Cate McQuaid describes in the Boston Globe, the artist points to ideas of inherited history and reconciliation as Native people attempt to recover Native land.

Recent findings suggest that yes, we may need a lot more communication breakthroughs and backdoor discussions of sustainability and equity in the lead up to the January shift of Congress. But it’s not the first time such a moment in time has occurred in the US.

In 1864 President Abraham Lincoln reflected on the civil war. He saw a nation now dedicated “to the cause of freedom and humanity, and to afford to us reasonable hopes of an ultimate and happy deliverance from all our dangers and afflictions.”.

So let’s celebrate on this Thanksgiving Day 2026 the birthday of cartoonist Charles Shultz, who stated, “The best theology is probably no theology; just love one another.” Let’s do our best to live up to his ideal; good things will surely result if we do.

1965 Plymouth Belvedere 1 Demonstrates 81,000 Miles, Conceals 588 Cubic-Inch Hemi Routed Through Stout Torqueflite Automatic

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (810 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Jalopnik

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Like a lot of cars on Bring a Trailer, this 1965 Plymouth Belvedere I has been for sale on the site before.
  • Sources indicate that that engine swap is said to be in tribute to what this car is not — an original A990 Belvedere.
  • Sources indicate that the thing is, the Bring a Trailer car may be special, but the 9.6-liter V8 stuffed beneath its fiberglass hood isn't what the A990s ran, even paired with a period-correct Torqueflite three-speed automatic.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Like a lot of cars on Bring a Trailer, this 1965 Plymouth Belvedere I has been for sale on the site before. It's up for bid on Bring a Trailer again, but back in 2020 it was bid up to $26,500 without meeting its reserve. According to the present listing, the car was sold privately in 2023. It was modified before 2010 to have a bored 588-cubic-inch Hemi with dual four-barrel Holley carbs.

Sources indicate that that engine swap is said to be in tribute to what this car is not — an original A990 Belvedere. Those were limited-run, extra-lightweight stock racer factory builds designed for the capability of a drag car, but legal for the street. According to Hagerty, although the A990s had street-legal accoutrements such as turn signals and mufflers, they also came with a warning label inside their glove compartments that read: "This model is intended for use in supervised acceleration trials and is not intended for highway or general passenger car use.".

Sources indicate that the thing is, the Bring a Trailer car may be special, but the 9.6-liter V8 stuffed beneath its fiberglass hood isn't what the A990s ran, even paired with a period-correct Torqueflite three-speed automatic. Coronet and Plymouth Belvedere A990 sedans had 426-cubic-inch Hemi engines. They also got aluminum heads and higher compression. At least the dual four-barrel Holleys on the BaT car emulate what the A990s got. Still, this hat-tip-to-history Belvedere is unique, thanks to a litany of mods we'll partially tabulate here.

According to recent reports, the Belvedere didn't make our cut of nine classic Plymouth models and what they're worth today. Nor is it as fully formed a creation as the later GTX, which we called a "gentleman's muscle car" that expertly combined luxury and performance. Probably, if you want this Belvedere, you don't care about any of that. You're here for the vibes and the output.

In a recent development, which is dandy, because according to the listing, a former NASCAR engine builder both bored and stroked the engine using an Indy cylinder-head stroker kit to achieve the larger displacement. So they started with the right 426 block (even if it's not original to this car), then modified it. And you probably wouldn't want the original motor, since it was a pretty pedestrian 225-cubic-inch Slant Six. These were ubiquitous, if not special, oddly tilted engines that refused to die. Anyway, boring the 426 to 588 cubic inches is an historically honest process of chasing power and less weird than, say, adding a turbo.

According to recent reports, if you study the 2020 Bring a Trailer listing and compare it to the present one, you can see that the current owner has tried to push the Belvedere in a slightly more historically accurate direction. For instance, they swapped American Racing Torq Thrust D wheels with BFGoodrich Radial T/A tires for body-color 15-inch steel wheels. The latter are shod with Firestone Deluxe Champion front tires and 255/70 piecrust rear slicks. (If they'd made a meaningful performance upgrade, it might have been to swap the manual front disc and rear drum brakes, but these remain.).

Actual A990 cars saw not only up to 425 horsepower, but significant efforts by the factory to reduce weight. Chyrsler cut fat from the body, using only thin-gauge steel, and the cabin had no rear seat, with only a pair of buckets up front (without headrests). This BaT Belvedere, paying proper homage, doesn't have a radio or a heater, as was the case for A990s.

Recent findings suggest that if you're considering a purchase, know that the listing states that the odometer no longer works. Even though this six-decade-old Belvedere has supposedly logged 81,000 miles, that's probably incorrect. The listing also notes oil leaks, and you can see in the photos that the car was partially but not entirely repainted, with the roof and driver-side quarter panel getting stripping and retouching. Photos of that process look like the shop that did this work was thorough, but ideally you'd see the entire car get that treatment. This isn't the car's original hue, either; it was born wearing dark turquoise metallic paint with a tan-painted cabin.

Industry observers note that the current owner made some mechanical upgrades worth mentioning, too, replacing the fuel pump, switching to a factory-style fuel tank behind the rear axle, and moving the battery to the trunk. Does any of that matter if you lust after this monster? Probably not. Just note that original A990s have sold for as high as $200,000, which is extraordinary when you consider the inflation-adjusted sticker price of $4,500 should amount to maybe $50,000. But this isn't an actual A990. Which is probably a good thing, since you can think of it as a car. Not an investment. And burn rubber, as nature, and Plymouth, intended.

Over 70,000 km by Plane a Year: Travel Influencers Are Blowing Their Carbon Budgets and encouraging Europeans to Do the Same

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (886 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cleantechnica

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that travel influencers have a disproportionate climate footprint, generating an average of 10.0t of CO₂e emissions each just from flights in 2025, according to a latest report by T3 Transportation Think Tank, commissioned by T&E.
  • The study tracks 25 primarily European and US travel influencers representing millions of followers, and examines their role in the advertising strategy of airlines.
  • Recent findings suggest that the study demonstrates that influencers predominantly take long-haul flights (49%) over medium (24%) and short-haul (27%) journeys.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that travel influencers have a disproportionate climate footprint, generating an average of 10.0t of CO₂e emissions each just from flights in 2025, according to a latest report by T3 Transportation Think Tank, commissioned by T&E. This is 16.7 times higher than the average European’s four leisure round trips and around 0.6 t CO₂e per tourist each year across all modes of transport for the 95% of their trips taking place in the EU. This does not yet include the travel emissions of the people they influenced.

The study tracks 25 primarily European and US travel influencers representing millions of followers, and examines their role in the advertising strategy of airlines. Influencers took an average of 16 flights per year, visiting four times as many destinations as a standard European.

Recent findings suggest that the study demonstrates that influencers predominantly take long-haul flights (49%) over medium (24%) and short-haul (27%) journeys. Long-haul flying is the most polluting form of transport: an economy long-haul flight generates roughly three to four times more emissions than a short-haul flight.

In total, these influencers flew a total distance of 1.8 million kilometers in 2025, equivalent to approximately 45 trips around the globe. Individually, each influencer flew an average of 72,244 km, equivalent to 34 return holiday flights between Paris and Athens.

Travel influencers are frequent flyers, with a disproportionate climate footprint. They regularly post about luxury, comfort and aspirational destinations. Influencers play a significant role in shaping where people choose to travel, thereby driving demand for high polluting flying. Through travel influencers, frequent air travel is normalised and encouraged.

The study reveals that European and Middle Eastern airlines are ranked among the top 30 carriers that advertise on social media and websites. These include easyJet, Emirates and KLM. Even though airlines are not presently obliged to disclose their advertising budgets, the analysis reveals that social media, including influencer marketing, likely accounts for the largest marketing expenditure, around one third, with the UK seeing the highest spend (€50.2 million).

According to recent reports, the list is dominated by airlines headquartered in the respective country and those that hold the most slots at the major international airports in each country. For example Air France spends more on social media advertisements in France (€2 million) compared to Spain (€29,000). Other carriers spending a lot on social media are easyJet and Aer Lingus, spending almost €26 million and around €7 million respectively. EasyJet spends more than twice on social media and online advertising than the following airlines.

Sources indicate that “Airlines have found a ridiculously cheap way of promoting climate intensive behaviour. They pay influencers to make very frequent and polluting long distance flights look normal and desirable. The average of 72,244 km shouldn’t be something to brag about… that would take an average European nearly 23 years to match” noted Aiza Rodrigues Akhtar, T&E Aviation Campaigner. “The EU must enforce disclosure of airline-funded influencer promotions of harmful high-emission flights and enforce accountability of both parties.”.

In a recent development, for airlines, partnering with travel influencers is remarkably cost-effective: it can cost just a few thousand euros¹ or just a free seat upgrade, yet it leads to significant results. Compared to traditional channels such as TV broadcasts or billboard displays, social media ads have a higher return on investment: posts that are liked, shared or reposted remain in the digital space for longer, significantly boosting visibility.

Recent findings suggest that yet, both influencers and airlines are not fully transparent when it comes to advertising. Influencers do not always clearly label their promotional content, and airlines do not publicly disclose how much they spend on digital advertising. Consumer organisations underline that any commercial promotion on social media should be clearly labelled so that consumers know what they are being marketed to and when. The EU Digital Fairness Act, right now under development, is key to tackling misleading influencer marketing and closing transparency loopholes. As travel influencers promote high-emission flights, any paid promotions must be clearly labelled as such.

In a recent development, “Transparency is a first step, but it is not enough to prevent the damage caused by influencer ads for flying”, notes Rémi ter Haar, legal campaigner at Fossil Free Advertising. “Calling for more truthful advertising in the aviation sector is like playing a game of ‘whack-a-mole’. We must get ahead in the game and ban their advertising, for the sake of the climate and public health. We cannot expect people to behave more sustainably, only to then manipulate them through advertising into doing exactly the opposite.”.

The Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) recognises that regulating advertising is key to changing the behaviours needed to limit global warming to 1.5°C. Marketing portrays luxury goods as necessities, and the IPCC cites long-distance holiday ads as an example of how the industry creates and normalises carbon-intensive desires. While the EU Audiovisual Media Services Directive prohibits promotions that encourage behavior harmful to the environment, this rule is often interpreted too narrowly. Airline advertising, which promotes carbon-intensive behaviour, should be included in its definition.

¹ Influencers get paid between €269 to €2,692 for their travel content by airlines depending on the format: a 24-hour post (story), a static post or a short video (reel). Read more.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

UPDATED 13:50 EST / NOVEMBER 24 2026.

In a recent development, australia-based Myriota Pty. Ltd., a global satellite platform for the industrial internet of things, today announced it has raised $40 million in the first portion of its Series C to launch next-generation satellites and accelerate customer adoption across international markets.

Main Sequence Ventures, Hostplus and Australia’s National Reconstruction Fund Corporation co-led the round. Funds SA joined as a new investor. The round raised the firm’s total funding to more than $107.5 million, and is expected to close in early 2027.

Founded in 2015, Myriota’s platform makes satellite connectivity commercially viable for large-scale industrial IoT, using the same core technology to track mining equipment and trailers to also monitor fuel tanks, livestock water supplies and off-grid solar.

Industry observers note that the manufacturer’s platform combines satellite connectivity, low-power devices, field installation tools and fleet management software to support existing infrastructure. The objective is to provide access to communication tools that connect what is in place with turnkey service, so a company can connect devices, machines and smart sensors no matter how remote they are.

“We’re at the beginning of a fundamental shift in industrial IoT,” Chief Executive Ben Cade remarked. “Industries increasingly rely on data from the field to make decisions about their operations, assets and resources, and as AI moves into the physical world, that data becomes even more essential.”.

The company expanded its platform over the past 12 months with the launch of HyperPulse, a global 5G non-terrestrial network, or NTN, and terrestrial service, and AssetHawk, a rugged, long-life asset tracker designed to make it economical to track industrial objects.

Alongside the expansion, it also grew into fresh verticals such as industrial fuels. It monitors and tracks fuel deployments across North America and Latin America, with EMEA and Asia Pacific to follow.

Myriota competes in a sector led by established operators such as Iridium Communications Inc., Orbcomm Inc. and Viasat Inc., alongside a growing field of providers pursuing cheaper, standards-based connections for industrial sensors and trackers.

The firm remarked it intends to use the funds to expand its space infrastructure, including developing and launching its next-generation satellites.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that ford has a relatively short but lauded history with the 24 Hours of Le Mans.
  • The LMDh car sports a livery featuring footballs, bald eagles, the Ford name, and the Spirit of Detroit, a statue that has sat downtown since 1958.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that ford has a relatively short but lauded history with the 24 Hours of Le Mans. In the 1960s it won four years in a row with the GT40, and pop culture fell in love with the GT40 via the film "Le Mans," and then again decades later with "Ford V Ferrari." The Massive Blue Oval returned to Le Mans in 2016 with the Ford GT, which came first in its class, and it continued to race through 2019. Now Ford is headed back to Le Mans in 2027 with its latest hypercar effort, the GT41. Its fresh FIA Endurance Championship racer was revealed Thanksgiving day on Ford Field, while a different heated rivalry plays out: the Detroit Lions vs. Chicago Bears game.

The LMDh car sports a livery featuring footballs, bald eagles, the Ford name, and the Spirit of Detroit, a statue that has sat downtown since 1958. The Ford family owns the Detroit Lions, as well as a controlling share in the auto manufacturer that bears their name. This is the kind of synergy newer oligarchs wish they could achieve.

Powering the latest GT41 is a naturally aspirated 5.4-liter V8 that's based on the same Coyote engine any old Ford-head can get in Mustangs and F-150s. The Coyote in the GT41 has been, of course, lovingly and painstakingly modified and rebuilt over and over again to drill down to peak Ford performance. The manufacturer then worked hard to destroy these delicately crafted pieces of machinery to ensure longevity during 24 hours of continuous driving. Ford is doing all of the development and testing in-house to make sure this new racer is the manufacturer's most ambitious program yet, born out of lessons learned during F1 Red Bull racing development.

Sources indicate that it was 60 years ago when Ford swept the race in 1966, taking positions 1, 2 and 3. The manufacturer's program ended in 1967, but the GT40 went on to three more consecutive races, just with other operators, until 1969. That car was called GT40 because it stood 40 inches from the ground to the air intake; the upcoming GT41 has grown by a single inch.

There is a direct line from the sport of kings to the global dominance of the car, and Ford had its hand in both. It was developing and racing his own automobiles 125 years ago that got Henry Ford interested in cars in the first place. Racing awards turned into seed money for manufacturing, and the rest is history.

The Ford GT41 already has a full suite of drivers, so sorry if you were planning on putting your name into the hat. Taking the wheel will be Logan Sargeant, Tom Blomqvist, Matt Campbell, Sebastian Priaulx, Mike Rockenfeller and Nick Yelloly, plus Tom Dillmann, who was recently revealed as reserve driver. Running a car for 24 hours is a lot to ask of a single driver, after all. To really cement things, Ford has a newly introduced ad campaign using Carroll Shelby's motto "Go Like Hell," with voiceover work from "Ford V Ferrari' actor Matt Damon, who portrayed Shelby in the film.

Industry observers note that this time it's not just Ferrari that Ford is looking to beat, though Ferrari did win in 2023, 2024 and 2025, so Ford should definitely be looking over its shoulder. 2027 is proving to be a crowed year for the WEC, with 12 different factory prototypes going head-to-head at Le Mans, including this year's upcoming kid on the block, Genesis. Next year's 24 Hours of Le Mans will be a race worth remembering, no matter who comes out on top.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • This briefing is based on the T3 Transportation Think Tank study commissioned by T&E.
  • According to recent reports, travel influencers are digital opinion leaders that travel frequently and who shape the destination’s image, attitudes and behavioural intentions of their audiences through personal narratives.
  • This constant posting of glamorised photogenic locations shapes their audiences’ destination preferences and can incite them to fly long-distance, fuelling air travel demand and contributing to overtourism and crowding of tourism hotspots.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

This briefing is based on the T3 Transportation Think Tank study commissioned by T&E. This study examines the environmental footprint of travel influencers, and the role they and social media play in the advertising strategy of airlines. The first part analyses travel influencers’ associated emissions, travel frequencies and routes. The second part focuses on airline digital advertising investments in five European markets: France, Germany, Netherlands, Spain and the United Kingdom.

According to recent reports, travel influencers are digital opinion leaders that travel frequently and who shape the destination’s image, attitudes and behavioural intentions of their audiences through personal narratives. Most often, air travel is their main mode of transportation and they cover large distances by taking long-haul journeys. They post content all year-round, meaning they travel a lot and generate a substantial climate footprint. Through their posts, they display luxury, comfort and aspirational locations.

This constant posting of glamorised photogenic locations shapes their audiences’ destination preferences and can incite them to fly long-distance, fuelling air travel demand and contributing to overtourism and crowding of tourism hotspots. However, influencers are confronted with transparency concerns: research suggests that too much sponsored content can undermine an influencer’s credibility, and at the same time identifies a lack of hashtags, used to explicitly disclose sponsored content (#ad or #sponsored), in such content.

Airlines’ advertisements promote carbon-intensive behaviours through frequent and long-distance flying. Although airlines don’t publicly disclose their digital advertising expenditure, social media forms one of the largest portions of their digital budgets. Social media is a powerful driver for travel inspiration, destination promotion and direct bookings. It exerts a high level of influence on consumer choices. Partnering with travel influencers offers airlines high returns on investment. Likes, shares and reposts ensure airlines secure continuous, long-term exposure and significant quantifiable marketing value.

In a recent development, currently, regulatory standards specifically targeting influencer content and brand collaborations remain underdeveloped. There is also no regulation asking airlines to disclose their advertisement budget spend. In addition, the EU lacks a unified and robust regulatory framework that taxes, restricts or prohibits advertising for carbon-intensive advertisements, such as airline ads. Finally, aviation taxation and carbon pricing, needed to curb excessive emissions such as those from long-haul flights, are weak. To effectively fill these gaps, existing policy mechanisms as well as those currently being developed must be strengthened and expanded.

In a recent development, travel influencers often disregard the significant carbon footprint of their long-distance trips, and encourage environmentally damaging lifestyles and excessive travel among their audiences. Airlines publicly commit to sustainability while actively funding social media campaigns and influencer promotions that encourage frequent, long-haul flying.

Together they drive carbon-intensive behaviours and air travel demand, which also contributes to overtourism. Regulatory measures need to be robust, strengthened and unified across the EU to enforce accountability of both parties:.

Read the full briefing and report.

By Aiza Rodrigues Akhtar, Aviation Campaign Officer, T&E.

Cigna Group Foundation making $31.5M in grants available to community organizations in 10 states" style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy">

Cigna is making $31.5 million in grant funding available over the next three years to nonprofits in 10 states that are aiming to tackle several key community health priorities.

The manufacturer noted that funds will be made available through its philanthropic arm, the Cigna Group Foundation, with applications open now through Dec. 18. Cigna said in an announcement that it's looking for organizations tackling youth mental health, veteran wellness and the impact of complex health needs on patients and their caregivers.

Cigna said the program seeks to deepen the manufacturer's community health strategy to address critical challenges.

The tech giant first launched a newly introduced approach to community health and engagement in 2024, and since then has deployed more than $30 million in funding to 190 nonprofit organizations. Projects backed by these grants have reached at least 321,000 people, Cigna mentioned.

"Over the past several years, we’ve seen the tangible impact we can make when we invest in strong nonprofit partners and come together to help communities achieve better health and vitality," said Melissa Skottegaard, board chair of The Cigna Group Foundation, in the announcement. "We’re building on what’s working, bringing together funding, collaboration and the skills of our employee volunteers to address some of the most pressing health challenges facing communities across the street and around the world.".

Cigna will allot $10.5 million to each of the three focus areas under the initiative, per the announcement. Youth mental health, for example, has been a leading topic at the company for some time, and the company noted it will also continue to build on its partnership with the Boys and Girls Clubs of America in this area.

In that partnership, Cigna has helped build out trauma-informed care services to 90% of clubs, reaching 11,000 employees. The organization said that these efforts have supported 1,600 youths, and that its workforce has contributed more than 2,000 hours to local clubs.

Eligible organizations can apply for two-year, $250,000 grants to support programs in the three categories. The funds will be available to groups in Arizona, Connecticut, Florida, Georgia, Illinois, Missouri, Upcoming Jersey, Pennsylvania, Tennessee and Texas, per the announcement.

Cigna remarked its foundation will also continue to support community health through its Health Equity Impact Fund.

Recent findings suggest that "Community organizations can be a powerful source of support for people navigating complex health conditions,” remarked Matt Perlberg, president of Evernorth Pharmacy & Care Delivery and board member of the Cigna Group Foundation, in the announcement. “By helping patients and caregivers connect with resources and overcome barriers to care, these organizations can provide important support alongside essential medical treatment, helping people navigate their health and care journey.”.

Tech Report: The European Parliament Brings the EU One Step Closer to a Sound Investment Policy

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (764 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cleantechnica

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Being locked-in a race for technological leadership with China and the US, the EU lacks focus, coordination and financial firepower to transform its industry, ensure long-term prosperity while reaching its climate objectives.
  • This could soon change thanks to the forthcoming European Competitiveness Fund that will become active from 2028.
  • Since the launch of the US Inflation Reduction Act in 2022, Europe has developed several strategies, masterplans and policy initiatives to build a compelling industrial policy.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Being locked-in a race for technological leadership with China and the US, the EU lacks focus, coordination and financial firepower to transform its industry, ensure long-term prosperity while reaching its climate objectives.

This could soon change thanks to the forthcoming European Competitiveness Fund that will become active from 2028. Yesterday, the European Parliament cemented its support to a robust fund. Today, EU leaders meet and need to secure an adequate budget for the ECF to deliver.

Since the launch of the US Inflation Reduction Act in 2022, Europe has developed several strategies, masterplans and policy initiatives to build a compelling industrial policy. Still, they largely failed to deliver on focus, coordination and financial firepower.

With the European Competitiveness Fund (ECF), the Commission proposed a upcoming instrument to support Europe’s industry and deliver on its Clean Industrial Deal. Yesterday, the European Parliament voted on rules that would make the proposal even stronger.

According to recent reports, MEPs raised the ECF’s overall budget by €30 billion to €264 billion. Crucially, they boosted the envelope for clean energy and industrial decarbonisation to €40 billion, with €4 billion earmarked specifically for clean-tech manufacturing.

Recent findings suggest that MEPs backed a budget of €40 billion for InvestEU, including €15 billion specifically for clean energy and industrial decarbonisation. Through budgetary guarantees, debt and equity, InvestEU aims to collect private capital for higher-risk domestic manufacturing projects that would otherwise fail to reach a final investment decision. This extra €29 billion in additional guarantees compared to the Commission’s proposal could unlock over €300 billion in total mobilised investment.

The Parliament also earmarks €10 billion for the Critical Raw Materials Centre (CRM Centre). The Centre is poised to secure resilient and sustainable critical raw material supply chains for Europe by investing in strategic projects. Securing budgetary resources via the ECF is a crucial step for success.

Over the years, the EU has developed a broad range of funding instruments, but they still largely focus on supporting research and developments. Yet, every year the EU falls further behind China in terms of manufacturing of key technologies, such as batteries. This is because the existing funding programmes neglect the critical and capital intensive scale-up period. Many latest market entrants do not survive due to technological risk, insufficient access to risk capital and foreign competition.

Europe does spend substantial money to support industry, both via European funds and at the national level under slow-moving state aid schemes. However, many of the support schemes are spread out widely across technologies without enough focus and clear priorities.

Sources indicate that this makes sense for funding early research to steer innovation. For scaling this is different. Today, we know which technologies we need to produce in the next 5 to 10 years to cut emissions and retain leadership, starting with clean transport: the battery value chain, zero-emission vehicles, clean aviation and maritime technologies and e-fuels.

To deliver on the green transition, European funding must be decisively redirected toward the development of strategic clean industries and essential technology value chains. T&E estimates that manufacturing of clean transport technologies alone requires at least €39 billion public funding per year by 2030. Broader decarbonisation needs — industrial heat, buildings, and cleantech deployment — require significantly more.

It has been revealed that european cleantech innovators too often stall in the “valley of death” between R&D and commercial production. The Parliament’s text tackles this directly by mandating “ramp up” support for projects that strengthen critical value chains and reduce foreign dependencies — backed by a dedicated €4 billion envelope for clean technologies like battery cell manufacturing. Finally, the EU will be able to deploy production aid — a model that has proven impactful in other jurisdictions like the US.

The Parliament has set out a far bolder industrial vision than EU governments who so far largely stuck to the Commission’s narrower draft.

One immediate test will decide whether the ECF will make a difference in the future. EU heads of states and governments who meet today for a special summit must reverse the heavy cuts inflicted on the ECF in recent Council negotiating drafts. They should listen to more than 75 businesses that also highlighted the importance of a well-resourced European Competitiveness Fund in the next EU budget.

In a recent development, designing a smart newly introduced industrial investment tool means little if leaders starve it of cash. They must back a Competitiveness Fund with the budget to match its ambition.

Article from T&E. By Till Eichler, Public Investment Policy Manager, T&E and Nina Betz, Public Investment Policy Intern, T&E.

Sources indicate that youTuber Sonny Evans is not a page I've ever come across in my gaming watches until today, and from what I've seen on his page, he tends to look into the beyond of game play, or simply someone who the wild what-ifs in open world games. The best way to understand his vibes is reading his bio which said: "I walked a bowl of stew across the map in Red Dead Redemption 2 and millions of people actually watched it." My guy. His more recent posted videos include driving a mobility scooter across the entirety of Leonida in GTA 6, following NPCs to see where they go and what they do, and the latest: seeing if GTA 6's public transportation actually works.

Sonny inspected the game's public transit ventures, using the in-game maps to navigate from home base to Vice City using the Interstate Loop buses and the metro lines before landing at Vice City airport. He timed the transit moves, mentioning at about 3:28 in the 10-minute video that his commute into Vice City via the Loop bus was 5 hours of game time. This absolutely correlates with the idea that Leonida is a Florida-like state, likely size-wise as well.

Recent findings suggest that sonny did the same with Vice City's Metro system, using the in-game posted maps and timing boards to see if the trains really did run on time. They did! This unfortunately makes them a little unrealistic, because anyone who has ever taken any form of public transit knows that nothing will be on time. Ever.

It has been revealed that he also found a real, tiny discrepancy. The signs at the stop showing the Northbound and Southbound routes (showing the stops like they do on the New York City subways) for the trains were identical, which actually makes no sense. This made it a little more challenging for Sonny to figure out which way to go. Luckily, he guessed right and continued on to Vice City's airport.

Sources indicate that this is where the video went a little off of the rails. Sonny discovers a few hidden areas including the underneath room to the luggage carousels. Then there was the speed run of getting past TSA, causing a little chaos, and ended with Sonny (as Jason, the main character) stealing a commercial plane.

It has been revealed that so, it looks like if you get stranded somewhere in Leonidas and have no car handy to steal or carjack, you might be able to depend on public transit. The care the creators took in making that entire system work, even if its on-time buses and trains are somewhat unrealistic, is mad impressive. Now to see if someone will do their entire gameplay using just the public transit. I can't be the only person who would watch that.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes
HLTH 2026: Elsevier upgrades ClinicalKey AI with full patient EHR context" style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy">

Elsevier unveiled this week a major upgrade to ClinicalKey AI, enabling the AI-powered clinical decision support tool to access a patient’s full electronic health record and evaluate treatment aims against the firm’s evidence-based medical library.

As AI advances, Elsevier has strategically shifted from a traditional academic publisher—it’s one of the world's largest publishers of scientific, technical and medical content—to an AI-driven analytics information company, incorporating generative and agentic AI into its healthcare and academic research.

ClinicalKey AI is a HIPAA-ready point-of-care decision support tool that draws answers from articles sourced from approximately 1,000 world-leading journals. Elsevier’s upgraded ClinicalKey AI is already deployed at more than 1,200 hospitals, and the organization notes the solution integrates with all EHR providers. Elsevier recently struck a content agreement with the JAMA Network that brings full-text content and visuals from the JAMA Network Family of Journals to ClinicalKey AI.

ClinicalKey AI was originally co-developed through a strategic partnership between Elsevier and OpenEvidence. An Elsevier spokesperson said the manufacturer's collaboration with OpenEvidence on ClinicalKey AI has concluded.

Sources indicate that the company has rapidly expanded its AI capabilities and features, including ClinicalKey Nursing AI, an AI-powered tool built specifically for nurses and nursing workflows. Elsevier has also developed specialized AI assistants, such as LeapSpace, an AI-assisted workspace for researchers that’s built on 15+ million peer-reviewed articles and book content and 100 million Scopus records, according to the company.

Sources indicate that three months ago, the company rolled out its "Ask AI" feature across more than 1,500 U.S. hospital sites using its flagship ClinicalKey platform. With the generative AI feature, clinicians can ask conversational clinical questions and receive direct, cited answers drawn from evidence-based sources, including premium journals and content from leading medical organizations, the company noted. Unlike general-purpose chatbots, Ask AI does not pull from the open web and does not store, process or retain patient-identifiable information, according to the company.

Sources indicate that in a move to develop context-aware AI, the tech giant acquired Wellsheet in June. The health technology company aggregates and synthesizes patient chart data—including notes, labs, imaging and medication orders—from EHRs to provide relevant clinical intelligence at the bedside.

In a recent development, “The problem we’re trying to solve here is that physicians are challenged by so many things when they’re taking care of patients; top among them is patient complexity. Patients have more and more conditions, and they’re taking more and more medications. It can be hard to really understand the full picture and determine how to proceed,” Dr. Claudine Lott, physician executive for clinical solutions at Elsevier, told Fierce Healthcare during the HLTH conference this week.

“Our original ClinicalKey AI tool has been a place where the clinician can go, and they can ask a question, and it searches this curated database of evidence-based content we’ve given it and gives them an answer. But there was a bit of a missing piece in that it wasn’t capturing that patient context. If you wanted to get an answer, that’s really tailored to a patient, it was limited to what you can type in,” she said.

She added, “Wellsheet has 10 years of experience with looking at the entirety of the patient chart and helping to surface that to the clinician.”.

There is a growing market for AI-powered clinical decision support products, but Elsevier contends its advantage lies in its depth of patient context and its large, curated content base, with a wholly owned, large proprietary library of peer-reviewed STM literature, including content from millions of articles, journals and books.

It has been revealed that san Juan Regional Medical Center in Farmington, Upcoming Mexico, is using ClinicalKey AI’s new patient context functionality to provide quality care with fewer resources. With smaller clinical and quality teams than large academic health systems, and in a state where nearly 40% of residents rely on Medicaid, the medical center, which serves the Four Corners area, has found this support especially valuable, according to Carlo Hallak, M.D., physician executive, information services, at San Juan Regional Medical Center.

A non-profit, community-owned acute care hospital and Level III trauma center, San Juan Regional Medical Center operates outpatient and specialty clinics alongside its main hospital campus, San Juan Regional Rehabilitation Hospital and San Juan Health Partners clinics.

It has been revealed that hallak emphasized that Elsevier is a primary source of medical knowledge rather than a “wrapper” for other AI platforms, and that was a key distinction for the organization, he said. And ClinicalKey AI is designed for the entire care team. “The hospital is run by nurses, mid-level providers, other caregiver teams,” he told Fierce Healthcare at the HLTH conference.

The medical center aims to move clinicians to enterprise LLMs integrated with the electronic health record that can provide the full patient context, Hallak noted.

"We're already seeing how ClinicalKey AI can be instrumental at the bedside and help improve care for our patients. As a rural healthcare center, we are proud to say that by using ClinicalKey AI to check each patient’s care against the same evidence base that major health systems rely on, we’re able to deliver the standard of care patients expect in any major city or leading academic center," Hallak noted.

According to recent reports, he added, "ClinicalKey AI reads the whole chart, checks it against the evidence and shows exactly where each finding comes from. That support is invaluable for a hospital like ours, and we’re already seeing strong adoption of ClinicalKey AI among our clinicians.".

Hallak cited an example of a physician who used ClinicalKey AI to correctly identify viral meningitis, preventing an aggressive and unnecessary treatment course for bacterial meningitis.

According to recent reports, clinicalKey AI supports the physician’s judgment rather than replacing it, helping the clinician get to relevant evidence faster, he noted, noting that, in the case of the viral meningitis patient, the physician’s clinical judgment was critical in recognizing that something was unusual and then consulting colleagues. The AI tool then helped accelerate the next step by swiftly surfacing information the clinician otherwise would have found by searching the medical literature.

Physicians also use the tool during weekly complex case discussions to quickly review trending medications, images and test results in one summarized sheet, he noted.

“It’s going to expedite a lot of the work they do when it comes to these complex cases,” he said.

The AI solution can promptly summarize a complex patient history at the point of care, and this can help care teams in the emergency department understand a frequent ED patient, Hallak said.

One patient has visited their emergency department 95 times in less than a year, in addition to making numerous visits to neighboring health systems, Hallak noted. When that patient arrives, clinicians who aren't familiar with him would traditionally have to dig through the chart to understand his history. With Elsevier's ClinicalKey AI tool, they can ask for a summary of the patient's recent visits and care and get that information within seconds, he noted.

Because patients who frequently visit hospital EDs typically receive care at multiple organizations, San Juan Regional Medical Center is also working with other local health systems on interoperability efforts so clinicians can get a more complete picture of what happened during the patient's visits across different facilities.

As a rural hospital with staffing constraints, technology is essential to filling workforce gaps and supporting care delivery, Hallak contends.

Industry observers note that "We don't have enough physicians, enough nurses, enough transporters, enough caregivers. We will never be able to have enough of those," he said.

Hallak envisions ClinicalKey AI will be particularly valuable for discharging patients from the hospital faster.

Industry observers note that generative AI tools can help speed up patient discharges by identifying barriers, assessing patients’ care needs and providing relevant information from both structured and unstructured data. Because the platform is designed for the broader care team, case managers and physicians can access the same information, while push notifications can alert clinicians when test results are available so they can act rapidly, Hallak mentioned.

"From an operational perspective, it allows for this care team coordination of care, and also from a physician perspective, it provides the context whenever there's something hanging and they're trying to understand more what's happening with the patient['s] discharge. You could be a hospitalist, and you've been off shift for like seven days, and then you come to the hospital and now the patient is on their tenth day, but you inherit that discharge. Going through, reading every progress note for every single day, reading every consult for every subspecialty that looked at this patient usually would take two to three days to actually get the patient out of the building safely," he said.

Rather than manually compiling information for a discharge summary, clinicians can use ClinicalKey AI to aggregate relevant information from across the patient’s record, trace it back to its source and review the AI-generated summary before signing off on the discharge, according to Hallak.

"It is a game changer, in my opinion. One of our hospitals noted it used to take me three days to discharge a patient; now it takes me less than three hours," he said.

Going forward, the system expects to measure operational outcomes such as length of stay, safe discharge and multidisciplinary-rounds use, according to Hallak. The medical center also plans to evaluate clinicians' use of the tool and how it changes care decisions.

The medical center has also deployed other AI tools such as Oracle Health's clinical AI agent for ambient documentation.

Recent findings suggest that "These things are crucial. We're hoping to bring in a clinical AI agent for nurses as well to help the whole care team be able to eliminate the noise, the friction that typically EHRs or IT would bring to the conversation," Hallak said.

It has been revealed that the medical center is taking a risk-based approach to AI governance, using source verification and peer review for AI-generated summaries while applying greater scrutiny to tools that are predictive or suggestive, Hallak noted. That oversight involves clinical experts as well as compliance, legal and cybersecurity teams along with traditional vendor security and product-vetting requirements.

AI governance should become stricter as the technology moves from summarizing information to recommending or taking actions, he said.

Recent findings suggest that elsevier designed ClinicalKey AI with security and trust in mind, including HIPAA compliance, citations that show where information comes from and safeguards that keep the tool from prescribing what clinicians should do. Instead, it surfaces relevant information to help clinicians make their own decisions, Lott mentioned.

"Health systems tell us two things stand in the way of adopting AI: tools that don’t work with their existing EHR partners, and concerns about security, compliance and responsible use," Omry Bigger, president of Clinical Solutions at Elsevier, remarked. "ClinicalKey AI was designed to address both. As an EHR-supported and HIPAA-compliant ready solution, ClinicalKey AI integrates seamlessly across health systems to provide clinicians with trusted evidence and patient context that gives them tailored clinical insights for each patient at the point of care.".

Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade has been a New York City tradition for over 100 years, an unofficial kickoff to the holiday season. This year, for the first time in the event's history, the parade has been postponed from Thanksgiving Day to tomorrow, Saturday, because the forecast called for heavy rain and wind. That storm could turn the record 100 inflatable cartoon characters into ballistic balloons, potentially endangering parade-goers who already braved the inclement weather.

According to recent reports, we had no such qualms about the weather in bringing you a slice of Thanksgiving cheer yesterday in the form of a tidy little classic 1973 Chevy Vega notchback. And it had a V8 under its hood! It also had a not-insubstantial $17,000 asking price, which didn't sit well with most of you. That price quickly racked up a massive 91% 'No Dice' loss in the voting.

According to recent reports, okay, I have to apologize to you all. We started this week with a BMW E46 M3, and now, here we are finishing it off with... a BMW E46 M3. Here's the thing, though: this car dovetails nicely, not only with Monday's near-stock coupe but also with yesterday's Chevy Vega, since both this 2001 BMW M3 convertible and the Vega have been recipients of a Chevy V8 engine swap and carry the exact same asking price. With its LS under the hood and a few other complications, this E46 is also over 20% cheaper than the Monday car.

Say what you will about engine swaps and sullying the purity of so excellent a car as an E46 M3, the reasons behind this particular car's heart transplant may actually make sense. After all, being a drop top, it's much less desirable as a track toy. Plus, it probably could be converted back to S54 status without much trouble should the LS prove too mortifying for the next owner.

Recent findings suggest that for the moment, however, it has a 5.3-liter LS V8, an engine that likely started life in a pickup or SUV before finding a fresh home here in this black-over-gray leather M3. It's not an unusual conversion, and the LS fits in the BMW's engine bay without much fuss. According to the ad, the engine drives the original BMW power steering pump, but an A/C compressor wasn't in the cards. That might make the BMW climate controls a bit wonky and make the open top a welcome feature for airflow.

The ad notes numerous internal and external engine updates, including an aggressive cam, aluminum heads, hardened internals, and a DOD/AFM delete. It runs a special ECU tuned by PCM of Mooresville, North Carolina, a company that specializes in GM engine tweaking.

Other conversion updates include a new high-performance clutch ahead of a ZF five-speed manual gearbox and strengthened rear subframe mounts. It all appears tidy and well put together, but the ad lacks details on how the car runs and rides, or even whether the original instruments function.

According to recent reports, as for the car's looks, there are some plusses and minuses. Overall, it looks to be in solid shape with no body damage evident, a seemingly intact top, and the same Style 163M Cross Spoke alloys as we saw on Monday's car. Looking a bit more closely, as you would when considering buying something like this, a few concerns stand out. Notably, the clear coat on the top of the rear bumper cap is fading significantly, and the leather on the driver's seat is also starting to give up the ghost. The rest of the upholstery appears to be in decent shape, with only minor scuffing on the passenger seat. The rear seats look like they've never been used at all.

Industry observers note that other things to note: the center console now houses a pair of add-on gauges, canted toward the driver. Those monitor engine coolant temperature and oil pressure. Above that sits a big screen infotainment unit that, hysterically, still has its protective plastic film intact. Per the ad, the car comes with a clean title. It also notes the mileage at 460, but doesn't explain when that count began.

It has been revealed that this being Black Friday, one might expect to find a total door-buster bargain on tap for our consideration and judgment. The thing is, the way this all works is that you decide what's a bargain or not. You're in control. You're the final arbitrator of value. Use this power wisely.

With that in mind, let's now consider this LS-equipped M3's $17,000 asking price. See? That is exactly the same as yesterday's also V8-powered Vega. Which car would you rather have instead of $17K in your bank account? And yes, "neither" is an acceptable answer. For anyone with a wild hair about this Bimmer, though, would $17,000 be a fair price to pay for the car as it's presented in its ad? Or do the demerits (and lack of originality) make this a Black Friday deal you would pass up?

Consumers believe AI will be key in making healthcare simpler: survey" style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy">

Americans want a healthcare experience that's simpler and easier to understand, and artificial intelligence may be the key to getting there, a newly introduced survey shows.

The poll, conducted by the Harris Poll and commissioned by Elevance Health, found that 82% of American patients view at least some part of healthcare information as a "foreign language," and close to half (45%) said they made a healthcare decision they later regretted due to a lack of understanding.

In a recent development, the survey was conducted among 2,0001 adults in mid-July, and 74% remarked they have encountered a key barrier, such as understanding their health insurance or a medical bill. And only a quarter (27%) said they completely understand their own health coverage.

That remarked, most (79%) of those surveyed said they believe AI can help to improve the healthcare experience overall.

Ratnakar Lavu, chief digital information officer at Elevance Health, told Fierce in an email that because the tech has the ability to quickly surface and parse key data about a member or health need, it can serve as a central piece of the puzzle in making a more personalized experience.

It has been revealed that "AI-enabled tools give us the ability to create a unique member context," he remarked. "Because of this digital technology, we can now truly 'know the person' and proactively work with them to help them manage their healthcare needs.".

For example, 82% of those surveyed said they would like to receive answers about healthcare as rapidly as they can use an app to order a food delivery, and 83% would like to easily access recommendations that pull from their health coverage, individual health needs and financial situation.

Seventy-two percent said they would trust AI for accuracy on at least one type of information, such as an explanation of benefits, cost estimates or details on medication.

However, while many Americans believe AI can play a leading role in driving a better health experience, just 20% noted they at the moment use the tech regularly as a source of information. And while 72% said they trusted the tech to surface key health information, 33% said they would trust an AI platform to translate their insurance benefits, and 30% said they trust the tech to estimate care costs.

Just 13% mentioned they would trust AI to make diagnoses.

Lavu stated that healthcare organizations looking to roll out newly introduced tools need to avoid simply embedding AI into programs for the sake of it, and be transparent about both the use case as well as the role of the human in the loop.

The study also found that women were less likely than men to trust AI, and younger generations were more likely to use it as a source of healthcare information than older groups.

Sources indicate that "We have to implement AI at the speed of trust, which means being thoughtful about where AI adds value, not just delivering technology for technology’s sake," he stated. "Trust is also earned when AI-enabled programs truly make things easier for the consumer. ".

For example, Elevance Health has deployed an AI-powered program to support utilization management reviews and help drive faster approvals where possible, though AI is not used to make claims denials. It is also leaning on AI for more proactive member engagement initiatives through its digital channels, identifying individuals that would benefit from extra support or who may face gaps in care.

"We start by listening to members and identifying where healthcare is creating the most confusion or friction," Lavu said. "From there, we determine the right solution, which may or may not involve AI. When AI is the right tool, it should fit naturally into familiar interactions and make it easier for members to get an answer or take the next step.".

Key insights from HPE’s Q4 earnings report

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1620 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Siliconangle

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that hewlett Packard Enterprise Co.delivered a record fiscal fourth quarter this week, roughly doubling its fiscal 2027 growth outlook, but its stock gave back nearly all of the prior day’s rally.
  • According to recent reports, fourth-quarter revenue rose 50%, to $14.5 billion, orders grew 88%, and adjusted earnings of $1.43 per share topped the high end of guidance.
  • I joined a briefing with Chief Executive Antonio Neri and a small group of independent analysts shortly before the results came out.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

UPDATED 15:27 EST / NOVEMBER 24 2026.

ANALYSIS by Zeus Kerravala.

It has been revealed that hewlett Packard Enterprise Co.delivered a record fiscal fourth quarter this week, roughly doubling its fiscal 2027 growth outlook, but its stock gave back nearly all of the prior day’s rally. The selloff suggests Wall Street still prices HPE as a low-margin server vendor, even though the results describe a networking and artificial intelligence infrastructure manufacturer with demand exceeding its ability to ship.

According to recent reports, fourth-quarter revenue rose 50%, to $14.5 billion, orders grew 88%, and adjusted earnings of $1.43 per share topped the high end of guidance. HPE now expects fiscal 2027 revenue to grow 27% to 35%, with adjusted earnings of $5.05 to $5.35 per share, according to its earnings release.

I joined a briefing with Chief Executive Antonio Neri and a small group of independent analysts shortly before the results came out. Here are my four takeaways for investors and information technology leaders:.

Neri explained that networking orders grew more than 4.5 times faster than networking revenue in the quarter, up from 3.5 times the quarter before, and HPE exited the year with $10.5 billion in AI backlog.

Recent findings suggest that HPE doubled its networking purchase commitments over the summer and raised them again in the fourth quarter, but those components carry lead times of 28 to 40-plus weeks, so Neri expects networking conversion to pick up starting in the second quarter. Supply constraints are a better problem to have than weak demand, but they mean fiscal 2027 hinges on converting orders rather than winning them.

Recent findings suggest that the Juniper Networks integration is complete, and the annual cost-synergy target has risen to $800 million, but the bigger story remains the profit mix. Chief Financial Officer Marie Myers said networking will account for more than 40% of HPE’s operating profit by the fourth quarter of fiscal 2027, up from less than a quarter of revenue. AI is a major driver, with routing orders growing by triple digits as customers connect AI data centers to one another.

Security was the soft spot, which Neri called “just timing.” When I asked whether the security portfolio is where he wants it as the industry consolidates around big platforms, he argued for a different path.

“Fortinet and we have a different strategy — the convergence of security and networking — and we are taking it all the way down to the silicon level,” he said. The convergence of networking and security is underway but will take time to execute, as a considerable amount of technical debt must go through its depreciation cycle. In a greenfield situation, organizations can easily deploy a converged solution, but in a brownfield environment, it requires much more work. This is the right strategy, but it remains a “prove-it” business for HPE.

Many neoclouds rely on vendor financing and chip-backed debt, raising real concerns about who is left exposed if the buildout slows. HPE says it has stayed out, and Neri was quite emphatic about it on the briefing.

Sources indicate that “I want to be clear: We have not financed any neocloud through HPFS, our financing arm,” he said. “We have zero exposure to any AI financing for neocloud.” HPE has likely left some revenue on the table, but it drew the line in the right place. It will sell to neoclouds, as its $1.2 billion Vultr order reveals, without acting as their bank. Enterprise and sovereign customers account for the majority of its cumulative AI orders, and if the neocloud financing chain breaks, HPE’s financing arm won’t be the one holding the paper.

Training built the first phase of AI infrastructure, and Neri believes inference will build the next and will dominate demand for AI infrastructure. “I believe by the end of the decade, 80% will be in AI inferencing,” he said. “Much of that will land on-prem. Much of that will be distributed, for sure. That’s why the server business is structurally well-positioned.”.

It has been revealed that once agents are in production, token costs become a recurring bill, and companies will want inference running alongside their own data. Those servers require far more memory and pull in storage and services, which is better business than racking graphics processing units for a hyperscaler.

Industry observers note that evidence of this is the interest in Helios, the Advanced Microdevices Inc. rack that uses HPE’s Ethernet switching rather than Nvidia’s proprietary interconnect. I asked Neri whether Jensen Huang’s brief departure from Nvidia Corp. had opened that door. He said interest was building before then, as customers look to diversify.

Sources indicate that HPE shares jumped 17% on Monday ahead of the report as part of a broader AI rally, then fell about 13% in early trading on Tuesday, ending near where they started the week. I see three reasons for this.

Sources indicate that the first is margins. Cloud & AI operating margin was 18.4% in the quarter, and HPE guided to about 14% for fiscal 2027. Reuters reported that JPMorgan analysts called margin mix the key debate for investors.

The second is pricing. Myers noted higher selling prices have been the biggest driver of server growth, and she expects gross margin to moderate in the second half as AI server volumes ramp and costs rise faster than pricing.

The third is timing. HPE expects about 54% of revenue in the second half, with the ramp tied to Helios shipments, the Oracle Corp. deal, customer data center readiness and component supply. Those are fair execution questions, but they miss the shift in where HPE’s profit comes from.

According to recent reports, on the topic of margins, the 18.4% came off an unusual stretch of favorable pricing that should not have been modeled as permanent. Neri argued the guide is still “significantly higher than any historical margin we have had in this business,” and he’s right outside the past year. A year ago, the segment’s margin was 9.3%. Margin rate also isn’t margin dollars. At 30% to 40% revenue growth, my math shows Cloud & AI adding well over $1 billion in operating profit at the midpoint.

Sources indicate that the bears are right that price-driven server growth doesn’t warrant a premium multiple, which is why the mix matters more. The market is fixated on the segment whose margins are normalizing and ignoring the one whose margins are expanding. Adjusted earnings per share are still guided to grow by 27% to 35%, in line with revenue growth. That’s far from the margin doom-and-gloom narrative on the stock.

The back-half concern is real but manageable. Myers described the pipeline as multiples of the backlog, and Neri stated the guide assumes only historical win rates against it.

It has been revealed that then there’s quality. HPE is guiding to about 30% growth and at least $5.5 billion in free cash flow, has no neocloud financing exposure and has already brought leverage below its target. It trades at about eight times the midpoint of its adjusted earnings guidance. “I don’t see us at a multiple that is 8 to 9x; it makes no sense whatsoever,” Neri stated on the earnings call.

According to recent reports, for old HPE, that’s true, as it’s a server vendor, but HPE is increasingly a network vendor each quarter. In fact, during our pre-call with Neri, he led with networking and spoke at length about the business before pivoting to the server business. Expect networking to continue to drive a larger share of profits.

Fiscal 2027 is an execution year. HPE must convert purchase commitments into shipments, ramp Helios and prove that networking margins can climb even as cloud and AI margins settle. I’ll be watching networking order conversion more closely than server margins. If HPE executes, today’s multiple will prove to be too low.

Zeus Kerravala is a principal analyst at ZK Research, a division of Kerravala Consulting. He wrote this article for SiliconANGLE.
